acceptance: Weekly Radar Domain exposes validated snapshot identity, as_of, universe snapshot identity, evidence cutoff, model version, and scoring version values without recalculating upstream facts.

WeeklyRadarSnapshot is an immutable metadata envelope, and WeeklyRadarPublication binds exactly one snapshot identity to ordered precomputed publication facts while rejecting duplicate fact identities.

The Weekly Radar Application layer defines a provider-agnostic WeeklyRadarPublisher port that consumes WeeklyRadarPublication and returns a typed boundary error without knowing Telegram, HTTP, persistence, credential values, or scheduling.

The new weekly_radar context has domain, application, infrastructure, interface, and acl layers; Domain and Application use only standard-library types and do not import other feature implementations.

Focused unit and integration tests cover blank-value rejection, snapshot metadata retention, publication-to-snapshot identity binding, ordered fact retention, duplicate rejection, and publisher-port compilation behavior.
The design spec and execution plan record the Weekly Radar boundary, future-WI exclusions, authorization, current-WI issue rule, and verification commands.
guidelines: New public APIs must be documented.
Keep Weekly Radar Domain and Application independent of external systems and other feature implementations.
A publication must remain bound to one immutable snapshot identity; delivery must not trigger recalculation.
Keep persistence, rendering, Telegram, Scheduler, retry, and receipt behavior outside this Contract.
Do not add dependencies for this Contract.
Resolve issues within the current Work Item when they remain inside its Contract scope; open a successor only for a distinct or materially expanded boundary.
Do not introduce trading, price prediction, target price, portfolio allocation, or capital-action behavior.

intent.problem: The repository has no typed Weekly Radar boundary that binds a publication to a historical snapshot while keeping calculation and delivery concerns outside the Domain.
constraints: Retain as_of, universe snapshot identity, evidence cutoff, model version, and scoring version as supplied snapshot metadata.
Publication facts are precomputed inputs; preserve their order and identity without calculating Top5, Stage Transition, Threshold Distance, Rising, Dropped, or System Health.
The Publisher port is provider-agnostic and must not import Telegram, persistence, scheduler, external access material, or runtime implementations.
intent.rationale: A stable Weekly Radar Domain Contract lets later Snapshot, read-model, renderer, publisher, retry, and scheduler WIs compose around one historical publication boundary without allowing channel code to redefine research conclusions.
